note: Mux walking in from the back room is routine and touches nothing Glitch cares about.
For an achievement- and power-driven Glitch with little care for strangers, Rogue handing him paid work worth a third of a sale is a modest step up, despite the dig about earning his keep.

With universalism and self-direction central, Rogue pressing him to unlock a thousand people's med files, kids included, for the Tiger Claws shows her as willing to prey on the vulnerable and to make him complicit.
A gain-minded Mux sees the man who owes him for two cells let a paying job lapse over scruples he does not share, which makes repayment less likely.
A benevolent Mux sees Glitch, broke and dependent on Rogue, still decline to sell out kids' med records, a decency that raises him.
A thrill-seeking Rogue with no concern for security likes Mux's nerve in treating a Militech sweep as a selling night.

For a Rogue for whom security and control are central, Mux heading off to run the back room all night during a full-kit Militech sweep invites the corp onto her grid, on his own call rather than hers.
A Rogue for whom benevolence and universalism matter most sees Mux refuse, on principle and at a cost, to sell people's kids' records to the Claws, a stand her own values respect.
For a power- and achievement-driven Rogue, her tenant turning down her business and lecturing her to her face undercuts her say and costs her the sale.
A universalist Glitch watches Mux stand up to the woman who runs his roof rather than sell kids' med files, which earns real respect.
A security-minded, conforming Glitch credits Mux's restraint from harming people, though crossing Rogue makes things less settled, so the gain is slight.
A benevolent, universalist Rogue hears Glitch offer free scrubs to everyone hurt in the clinic breach, which is plainly good of him.

For a Rogue who puts security and control first, a runner hiding from heat on her leave announcing that he will run corp-list scrubs from her booth tonight, without asking, draws attention and goes past her say.
A tradition- and conformity-minded Mux sees Rogue publicly uphold that debts get paid and back his claim against Glitch.
A Mux whose benevolence is central watches Rogue air a regular's debt to the room and cut him off while his deck is dying, taking the decision out of Mux's hands.
Mux offering the cell his failing deck needs is a kindness to a security-minded Glitch, tempered because taking it right after Rogue's ban puts him at odds with the woman sheltering him.
For a Glitch for whom achievement and power are central, Rogue offering the job that would make his name with every fixer on the strip is a real opportunity, and a sign she rates him.
A security-first Glitch who is lying low hears Rogue push him to hit a Militech payroll node alone tonight, which puts him in serious danger.
An ambitious, gain-driven Mux hears Glitch offer half a crate of Militech cells, far more than the debt, which shows him as a useful partner.
A tradition- and security-minded Mux sees Glitch dodge his debt and pitch a theft from Militech, which is both improper and risky.
Rogue learns Glitch quietly found and killed a Militech tracer on her line, protecting her and her bar.
Mux could not hear the whisper, so nothing reaches him.
Glitch saying he is going to see Mux and leaving is routine to Rogue.
A Mux whose benevolence is central is moved that Glitch, on the run, came in person to own the unpaid debt, apologize and thank him.
For a gain-driven Mux with no benevolence, this means two cells written off and a regular customer gone, and the apology is worth nothing to him.
For a Mux who holds to custom, leaving a debt unpaid breaks the norm, though the honest, respectful goodbye softens it.
A tenant reporting a leak is routine landlord business for Rogue.
Rogue fixed the leak and cut his rent by a quarter for the lost stock, a fair and generous landlord in the eyes of a Mux who values security and good custom.
For a security-first, conforming Glitch, Rogue turning down his last valuable and asking only that he keep his head down is safe, generous shelter on terms he is glad to keep.
An ambitious, independent Glitch hears Rogue order his deck dark and him sidelined until she says otherwise, which stalls his rise and puts him under her control.
For a Glitch whose self-direction is central, her refusing his stim is kind but comes with orders to stay dark until she says, so the control slightly outweighs the kindness.
From Mux's side Glitch only passed through the back room; nothing else reached him.
For a Rogue who values security and power, Glitch turning the Claws away from her door and onto the fence who was cheating her regulars protects her and removes a rival.
A universalist, benevolent Rogue is uneasy that Glitch saved himself by setting a gang on another man, though Dace was harming her regulars and her door is safe, so the drop is slight.
A Rogue who values benevolence and universalism sees Glitch help her while promising to warn anyone who was scraped, which fits her values.
For a power- and security-driven Rogue, Glitch attaching his own conditions to her shard and planning to tell everyone on it threatens her control of the asset and her deal.
An ambitious Glitch hears that Mux got him top-paying work that would make his name, which makes Mux worth more to him.
For a Glitch who is lying low with heat and puts security first, Mux handing his name to the Tiger Claws without asking exposes him to a gang.

For a security-first Rogue, Glitch killing a Militech tracer aimed at her bar is a real protection, but he burned her relay on his own call and left her dark for three days, so the net gain is slight.
A gain-driven Mux is paid in full plus one cell extra by a runner who can pull payroll jobs, which outweighs the risk of hot scrip.
For an independent, ambitious Glitch who wants power, a word of praise is outweighed by Rogue claiming his deck, his jobs and the first cut.
Mux ordering his usual drinks is routine.
Mux lied to three Claws holding Glitch's picture to cover for him, a real protection that keeps Glitch free and in business.
Glitch threatened to burn Mux alive among his crates, which makes him a direct threat.
